items.title: 🔴 LIVE:  Karnataka's KWIN City Chip Park Opens in December | AMD | Front Page
items.summary:
Karnataka's 200-acre semiconductor park at KWIN City near Bengaluru will become operational in December, building on ₹23,000 crore in state investments as the state expands its technology economy beyond Bengaluru and positions itself as a major destination for global chipmakers. 

This is your Front Page LIVE, bringing you sharp analysis of India's semiconductor revolution, nuclear energy ambitions, AI infrastructure and the technology developments shaping the country's economic future.

Today on Front Page LIVE:
- Karnataka's 200-acre KWIN City semiconductor park near Bengaluru is set to become operational in December
- India targets five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033 as part of a ₹20,000 crore push towards 100 GW of nuclear capacity by 2047
- Austin Lyons, semiconductor analyst at Creative Strategies, joins Supreeth Koundinya to discuss AMD's next-generation CPU strategy, NVIDIA's competitive position, and the Cerebras announcement
- Mysuru's digital economy reaches $1.3 billion as Beyond Bengaluru growth, startup expansion and global investment reshape the city
- Ashok Chandak, CEO and President of IESA and SEMI India, discusses India's shift from semiconductor design towards sovereign chip manufacturing and global supply chain partnerships
